stem: How long should a child with bacterial conjunctivitis typically be kept home from daycare or school?

options.text: For 3 to 4 days until a full course of treatment is delivered.
Until the eye is no longer red, usually within 24 hours of starting drops.
For 10 to 12 days to match the incubation period of the bacteria.
There is no need to stay home if topical ointment is used at night.

explanation: The lecturer recommends 4 days of treatment and staying home for 3 to 4 days to prevent the spread of the infection to others.
rationale: The timeframe corresponds with the duration of the prescribed antibiotic course.

optionExplanations.A: The lecturer recommends 4 days of treatment and staying home for 3 to 4 days to prevent the spread of the infection to others.
optionExplanations.B: Clinical improvement doesn't mean the child is no longer infectious; a full course of treatment is necessary.
optionExplanations.C: This period is too long for standard bacterial conjunctivitis; 4 days of treatment is the standard cited.
optionExplanations.D: Bacterial conjunctivitis is highly infectious, and children should be kept home to protect others in a group setting.

source.hint: The timeframe corresponds with the duration of the prescribed antibiotic course.
